children: SYDNEY--Consumer inflationary expectations across the Australian economy hit their highest level since May last week, strengthening the case for the Reserve Bank of Australia to raise interest raise another notch.

Weekly inflation expectations ticked up 0.1 percentage points to 6.3% over the week, while the four-week moving average rose 0.1 percentage points to 6.1%, according to a weekly survey by the ANZ Bank and pollster Roy Morgan.
The data comes after Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia, Andrew Hauser, said the inflation outlook has become "materially worse."

Financial markets are now bracing for the release of third-quarter inflation data on Wednesday, with any sign of further increase in price pressures set to clear a path to the RBA's fifth interest rate rise this year at a policy meeting next week.
The RBA targets inflation at around 2.5%, and it is currently running at close to 4.0% on-year.

Hauser also highlighted that the RBA's business liaison suggests that firms are increasingly willing to pass on higher costs to consumers, fanning fears that elevated inflation expectations are becoming embedded.
The survey data also showed consumer confidence rose 0.2 points last week to 67.9 points, a reading which is still around the lowest on record.
The four-week moving average for consumer confidence dropped 0.6 points to 67.7 points, the survey showed.
Australian consumers are currently feeling the sting of higher interest rates, soaring fuel costs, and a big retreat in house prices.
A further rise in interest rates would likely accelerate the retreat in house prices, while stoke reports of business failures.
The survey's time to buy a major household item subindex fell 6.3 points last week.
The weekly ANZ-Roy Morgan Australian consumer confidence rating is based on 1,073 interviews conducted online and over the telephone during the week to Sunday.
